metric.capability_coverage.basis_note: This capability_coverage figure uses the full fixed 88-point denominator per capability_universe.json 'capability_coverage.formula'; it is independent of the common-basis vs all-fragments distinction used for metrics A-D.
metric.capability_coverage.formula: C = 100 * (sum over 44 probes of capability_points * support_factor) / 88
metric.capability_coverage.na_policy_note: No probe was scored NONE for Go in this analysis; all 44 probes have a documented Go fragment path (FULL or PARTIAL). Per NA-1/NA-2/NA-3, the fixed 88-point denominator is unchanged regardless of support level, and every PARTIAL is recorded with its P-letter(s) and a citation rather than being excluded or marked N/A.

per_probe_support.note: `const n = 7` is a never-reassignable local binding; `return n` produces it. Builds/runs under `go build`.
Package-level `var counter int64 = 0` (mutable) plus `const LIMIT int64 = 100` (true compile-time constant, distinct construct from var).

`var v int32` declares without an initializer expression; two-way branch assigns 5/9 on both paths; read/return v. Delivers all numbered sub-requirements (Go's zero-initialization under the hood is a hidden-cost fact, scored under metric D, not a support criterion per support_rubric.determinacy_is_not_a_support_criterion).

Go has no documented mechanism for storage whose contents are specified as unspecified/uninitialized; arrays/slices are always zero-initialized per the Go language specification. R9-named substitution: fragment uses `var buf [16]byte` (default-initialized) instead of genuinely uninitialized storage.
`x++` (Go increment statement) is the fewest-token in-place update form.
`xs[1] = 42` mutates the slice's backing array in place; observable through the same slice header `xs`.
`port := &slot; *port = 9; return slot` — Go pointers give a second name with write access to the same storage.

Go re-slicing (`window := xs[0:]`) gives a genuinely non-copying view, but Go has no read-only/immutable slice type — the view remains mutable. Substituted weaker mechanism: a mutable non-copying view stands in for the demanded read-only view.

`first := &Obj{id:5}`; route through a one-element `[]*Obj{first}` and read back as `second`; `same := first == second` uses Go's pointer identity comparison (`==` on pointer types compares addresses per the Go spec), distinct from field/value equality.
Ordinary bare call `f(x)` where x is a slice; builds and runs under the frozen recipe.
`func put(p *int32){ *p = 12 }`; caller does `put(&cell)`; explicit `&`/`*` pointer form is Go's documented mechanism for a callee to write a caller's scalar local.

`neg := func(a int32) int32 { return k - a }` is a closure capturing enclosing local k; Go standard library has no generic slice-map function, so the canonical_task's own permitted fallback (ordinary iteration referring to `neg` by name) is used, which is explicitly allowed by the probe text, not an R9 substitution.
`func mid(xs []int32) int32 { return xs[1] }`; call site binds y; return y.
Go has native multiple return values: `func divmod2(a,b int32)(int32,int32){ return a/b, a%b }`; `q, r := divmod2(a,b)`; `return q+r`.
`r := a*b + c` with ordinary Go operator precedence.
`q := a / b` (truncating toward zero per Go spec), `m := a % b` (sign follows dividend), `d := float64(a) / float64(b)` (Go requires explicit conversion for mixed-type division).

per_probe_support.family: 8. integer overflow, division-by-zero, other numeric edge behavior
per_probe_support.note: Go has no checked/wrapping/saturating standard operations, so the plain `+` operator is used (rung iv); its overflow behavior (two's-complement wraparound) is defined by the Go language specification itself, satisfying 'determined by the operation itself'.

per_probe_support.family: 8. integer overflow, division-by-zero, other numeric edge behavior
per_probe_support.note: Rung (ii): explicit guard `if b == 0 { q = 0 } else { q = a / b }`, since Go has no standard checked-division operation.
`eq := s1 == s2` — Go strings are immutable value types and `==` compares contents per the Go spec, not identity.
`sort.Slice(xs, func(i,j int) bool { return xs[i] > xs[j] })` supplies an explicit descending comparator (standard library `sort` package); `lt := a < b`.
Go forbids implicit narrowing; rung (ii) explicit conversion `small := int32(big)` is used and documented (modular truncation per the Go spec).
`sum := float64(i) + d` — Go requires the explicit conversion `float64(i)`; no implicit numeric conversion exists in Go.
`e := xs[i]; return e` — ordinary Go slice indexing panics at runtime on out-of-range index (documented behavior); no separate checked form needed for the primary fragment.
`part := xs[1:4]` — Go slicing shares the underlying array with the source slice; no element copy.

R9-named substitution probe. Go has no Optional/nullable value type with a standard coalescing form; substitute uses `var o *int32 = nil` plus a hand-written if-statement for the fallback, since Go provides no default/coalescing operator for optionals.
R9-named substitution probe. Go has no optional-aware chaining/mapping/safe-call operation; substitute uses an explicit nil check instead of chaining.

per_probe_support.family: 13. errors, failure values, exceptions, and propagation
per_probe_support.note: `strconv.Atoi` returns `(int, error)`; `parse_twice` propagates via Go's documented explicit early-return-of-error-value idiom.

per_probe_support.family: 13. errors, failure values, exceptions, and propagation
per_probe_support.note: `n, err := strconv.Atoi(s); if err != nil { n = 0 }` is Go's normal if-error local-handling construct, explicitly listed as an acceptable form.

per_probe_support.family: 14. alternatives / sum / variant types and dispatch
per_probe_support.note: R9-named substitution probe. Go has no closed sum-type/algebraic-data-type construct; substitute is an interface implemented by two structs (Circle, Rect), which is an open hierarchy rather than a language-enforced closed alternative set.

per_probe_support.family: 14. alternatives / sum / variant types and dispatch
per_probe_support.note: Go type switch over the Shape interface with no default arm computes area for Circle/Rect; exhaustiveness-checking is scored under metrics B/D, not support (support_rubric.determinacy_is_not_a_support_criterion).

per_probe_support.family: 14. alternatives / sum / variant types and dispatch
per_probe_support.note: Go's structural interfaces are natively open to extension: a separate package defines `Tri` implementing `Shape.area()` without modifying the `shapes` package; dispatch through the interface reaches it. Built under toolchain_binding.multi_unit_recipes (`go build ./...`).
Go 1.18+ generics: `func head[T any](xs []T) T { return xs[0] }`, instantiated at []int32 and []string with declared result type T (not erased to interface{}).

Standard library `cmp.Ordered` (Go 1.21+, package `cmp`) is a genuine declaration-site constraint: `func max_of[T cmp.Ordered](a, b T) T`. Since Go genuinely has this capability, the named-substitution clause for F15.P2 does not apply.
`[]Named{A{}, B{}}` holds two concrete types behind interface `Named`; `items[0].tag()` dispatches at runtime to A's implementation. Idiomatic Go interface polymorphism.

`xs := []int32{1,2,3}`; Go standard library has no generic sum/reduce function for slices, so the canonical_task's own permitted fallback (explicit `for _, v := range xs { total += v }`) is used, not an R9 substitution.

`mp := map[string]int32{"a":1}`; range-iterate to sum values; `miss := mp["b"]` already yields the int32 zero value 0 for the absent key (Go map indexing's documented default-value behavior), satisfying the lookup-with-default form.
`f, err := os.Open("data.txt"); ...; defer f.Close()` — Go's documented `defer` guarantees the deferred call runs when the enclosing function returns, including on the error path.

Named final-clause substitution. Go has no deterministic end-of-lifetime hook (`runtime.SetFinalizer` is explicitly documented as best-effort/nondeterministic GC-timed). Substitute: an explicit `release()` method invoked via `defer` inside an immediately-invoked function literal acting as the scope, which is Go's nearest standard scoped-cleanup construct.
`import "fmt"; fmt.Println("x")`.

Package `util` exports `PubAdd` (capitalized identifier) and keeps `secret` unexported (lowercase); Go's capitalization rule is a compiler-enforced package-visibility boundary. Built under toolchain_binding.multi_unit_recipes (`go build ./...`).
Two goroutines send results on channels; `sum := <-ch1 + <-ch2` joins both. Goroutines/channels are Go's standard concurrency facility.

`sync/atomic` (`atomic.AddInt64`) is documented to perform an atomic read-modify-write; two goroutines each add 1 to the counter 1000 times, joined via `sync.WaitGroup`; final value deterministically 2000.
Go's built-in `cgo` mechanism (`import "C"`) is part of the standard Go toolchain and allows calling the C standard library `abs(int)` without a third-party package or separate build system.

Exporting a C-ABI symbol named exactly `add2` requires cgo's `//export` pragma together with `-buildmode=c-archive` or `-buildmode=c-shared`, a build mode outside the frozen recipe (`go build -o BIN FILE.go` produces a plain executable with no such unmangled exported symbol). The mode ships with the standard Go toolchain and needs no extra download, so this is a P-b flag/mode deviation, not a NONE.

toolchain_recipe_used.multi_unit_recipe: go build -o BIN ./... (run inside a directory containing go.mod and a util/ package)
